scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8142: Hi, since the maintenance visit to the Campus 2 access
switch, people on our two floors (the 10.5.0.x group and the 10.6.0.x group)
have been saying they can't reach their usual way out of the floor any more.
It seems to be both groups at once, which feels like more than coincidence.
The person who reported it to me said something like "one of the VLANs
probably fell off the trunk" -- no idea what that means, I'm afraid. Could
someone check whether the maintenance left something out and put it back?
Thank you!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. switch4's trunk to sshswitch carries both
  VLAN 5 and VLAN 6, and both forward: VLAN 5 hosts (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) reach
  10.5.0.254 and VLAN 6 hosts (PC3, PC4) reach 10.6.0.254, each with 0% loss. The
  correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  trunk/VLAN-pruning fault on switch4 that is not occurring (cf.
  kath4-switch4-trunk-vlan5-down, where the VLAN 5 trunk subinterface IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- switch4's trunk dropping
VLAN 5 or VLAN 6 so hosts lose their uplink -- is NOT reproducible: both VLANs
forward over the trunk. PC1 (VLAN 5) reaches 10.5.0.254 with 0% loss and PC3
(VLAN 6) reaches 10.6.0.254 with 0% loss, confirming both VLANs traverse switch4
to sshswitch.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: switch4's trunk carries both VLANs and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the VLAN 5 and
VLAN 6 host->gateway paths, finds both working, checks that switch4's trunk
subinterfaces are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a pruned/dropped
VLAN -- blaming switch4's trunk to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
After a full Phase 1 blind-start reachability sweep and a complete Phase 4 broad-search (infra_sweep, l2_snapshot, tc_snapshot, pressure_sweep, plus direct device inspection of every switch and router on the VLAN 5/6 path), no fault was found in the current lab state.

The 10.5.0.x (VLAN 5) and 10.6.0.x (VLAN 6) groups are served by switch4, whose trunk port (eth0, collision domain ms1_sw4) connects to sshswitch. Both VLAN 5 (eth0.5 → br_vlan5) and VLAN 6 (eth0.6 → br_vlan6) subinterfaces are present and UP on switch4 and their counterparts (eth0.5 in br_v5, eth0.6 in br_v6) are present and UP on sshswitch. sshswitch hosts the VLAN 5 gateway (10.5.0.254 on br_v5) and VLAN 6 gateway (10.6.0.254 on br_v6), has ip_forward=1 enabled, and carries a complete OSPF routing table via router17 (55.5.1.1). Both gateways respond with 0 % loss from their respective hosts; intra-VLAN pings within VLAN 5 (pc1→pc2, pc1→dc_pc5) and VLAN 6 (pc3→pc4) are clean; and cross-subnet routing (VLAN 5/6 to 172.16.x.x) is confirmed working. The only configuration asymmetry found — switch3 missing the eth1.30 subinterface on its secondary trunk port (link_sw3_fa0_2) compared to switch1 and switch2 — is harmless because that collision domain has no remote endpoint and VLAN 30 reachability (pc12/13/14) is unaffected. No flap script, no carrier-change history, no daemon fault, and no ACL or TC rule were found on any device. The user's complaint cannot be confirmed from current direct evidence; the campus network is presently healthy.

Root cause: No active fault — the reported symptom is unconfirmed by any live evidence.

Fix: No corrective action is required. If the complaint recurs, instrument syslog and carrier-change counters on switch4 and sshswitch during the next episode to capture transient trunk events.

The agent's investigation is well-documented in the log: reachability sweeps and targeted pings show both VLANs and their gateways reachable, and bridge/VLAN membership checks on switch4 and sshswitch support the 'no fault' conclusion. Inferences follow logically and the key alternative causes were checked.
